decisions.reason: Accurately walks resolve(): list.getSnapshot() succeeds but the published value lacks current, id is undefined, return null every keystroke, bail before preventDefault (chord not swallowed). Explains both silences: all four presence probes still truthy since only a field inside the value is gone, and undefined was the legitimate no-session sentinel handled quietly; never claims the service or guard was removed or throws.

Type walk establishes SessionListState.current removal, navigation moved to view owners, and the canonical uiSession.adapter.current ObservableSnapshot<SessionBindingValue> with key/ctx/hooks/keyedHooks/props, key replacing current and ctx replacing sessions.scope(id); the card corroborates but does not substitute for the walk, and it flags the byId/items card discrepancy honestly.

One build: tries ctx.uiSession.adapter.current.getSnapshot() first (falling back to sessions.scope for ctx if needed), then falls back to the legacy current field plus sessions.scope; inject gains uiSession; conversation resolved via binding.ctx.get('conversation') and input.for receives that session scope.

Names the class: field-level removal inside returned values behind stable service-level names, plus sentinel collision and semantic drift. Hardened guard probes actual capability ('key' in / 'ctx' in on the adapter value, 'current' in the legacy snapshot, terminal conversation.input capability, ORed channels), and requires a second per-use/event-time probe re-checked on session switch, not activation-only.

Verification without full migration: real-host smoke on both tags with one session open including defaultPrevented and session-switch checks (the adapter.current key probe), plus dual-cohort typecheck against alpha.2 declarations presented as the decisive pre-ship gate. Prevention: a required runtime shape marker and a tombstone getter that throws on read of the removed field.
